findings.title: iOS checkout/payment broken in Paris and Amsterdam since 14 Oct
findings.evidence: SQL check: Paris iOS checkout-to-order 62.0% \u2192 22.0% (25,731 checkouts), Amsterdam 61.9% \u2192 22.1% (11,350). London iOS 61.8% \u2192 62.2%. Payment-problem comments: Paris 12.1% (26/214), Amsterdam 15.5% (33/213), vs about 2.5% elsewhere. Lost revenue about \u20ac976k/month in Paris and \u20ac428k in Amsterdam (AOV about \u20ac60). Amsterdam NPS fell from \u22121 to \u221217.

findings.title: Barcelona organic search fell about 38% after a site change
findings.evidence: Sessions dropped from 83.7k to 54.8k in one week (week 38) and have stayed at about 50k. Revenue is about \u20ac40k a week below before, roughly \u20ac170k a month. Website-UX comments are 16.7% (37/221) vs 3.8% elsewhere, with customers reporting Google links that error and site search not working.

findings.title: The mix model says Google brand and Meta retargeting are saturated, while TikTok, creators, affiliates and YouTube are under-funded
findings.evidence: Extra revenue per extra euro: Google brand \u20ac0.07\u20130.62 and Meta retargeting \u20ac0.13\u20130.80 in Europe and New York, vs TikTok up to \u20ac8.08, creators up to \u20ac5.88 and affiliates \u20ac6.44. Model fit is good (R\u00b2 \u2265 0.7) on 24 of 44 market-lines. The plan's gain at unchanged spend is about \u20ac135k revenue a week, of which \u20ac62.7k a week is on long-history, good-fit lines.

findings.title: Paris Home captures only 64% of its search demand
findings.evidence: Paris Home makes 14.24 orders per 1,000 category searches vs 22.11 for peers. Other Paris lines capture 89\u201392%. An extra euro returns about \u20ac2.60 (4th best of 44 market-lines), and \u20ac6.44 on affiliates. Part of the gap is the checkout fault.

findings.title: Rain raises Home and Gifts demand and lowers Fashion drops
findings.evidence: Gifts: Paris +32.8%, Milan +31.8% [28.1, 35.6], Berlin +27.2% [24.0, 30.6]. Home: Barcelona +17.7% [14.8, 20.7], London +17.1%. Fashion drops \u22124% to \u221214% in every market. Beauty's effect is under 4%, which is within model error. Based on 229\u2013434 days per market-line.

findings.title: Milan late deliveries are hurting repeat buying
findings.evidence: Late-delivery comments are 24.2% (54/223) vs 6.4% elsewhere, starting the week of 5 Oct. Repeat share is 8.1% vs 11.3% in the prior period and 11.5\u201313.3% for peers. About \u20ac77k a month at stake (estimate).

findings.title: London overspent October by 22.5%
findings.evidence: \u20ac441,179 spent against \u20ac360,000 budgeted. The current run rate is \u20ac419.7k a month. Spend is up 14.9% over the last 28 days while paid revenue rose only 3.4%.

findings.title: Mexico City launch is far behind earlier launches
findings.evidence: Revenue is \u20ac1,999 a day, 5% of the earlier launches at the same age. CPA is \u20ac36.30 vs \u20ac19\u201322 for peers. About half of search demand is captured. Brand-distrust comments are 14.5% of feedback.

recommendations.action: P0 engineering fix for iOS checkout and payment in Paris and Amsterdam
recommendations.why: On 14 Oct the iOS checkout success rate fell from 62% to 22% in both markets, across all lines. Other devices and other markets were unaffected, and payment complaints rose about 5\u00d7 at the same time.
recommendations.expected_impact: Brings back about \u20ac1.4M of revenue a month (Paris \u20ac976k, Amsterdam \u20ac428k).
recommendations.how_to_measure: iOS checkout-to-order for Paris + Amsterdam over the last 7 days should return to about 62%.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT 1.0*SUM(orders)/SUM(checkouts) AS value FROM sales_daily WHERE device='ios' AND market IN ('Paris','Amsterdam') AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM sales_daily),'-7 days')

execution.note: Markets: Paris and Amsterdam, all lines. iOS checkout-to-order went from 62.0% to 22.0% on 2026-10-14 (Paris 5,657 orders from 25,731 checkouts; Amsterdam 2,504 from 11,350). London iOS is at 62.2%, and Android and desktop are at about 62%. Customers report cards declined and the payment page freezing on iPhone. Check the payment SDK, 3DS, PSP and Apple Pay releases from 13\u201314 Oct, and roll back if needed. About \u20ac1.4M of revenue a month at stake.

recommendations.action: Apply the mix model's channel split across the whole portfolio, with no channel moving more than 25%
recommendations.why: Google brand and Meta retargeting return well under \u20ac1 per extra euro, while TikTok, creators, affiliates and YouTube return \u20ac3\u20138. The model fits well on 24 of 44 market-lines. The 25% cap limits the risk on poorly fitting lines and keeps the plan inside its own limits (uncapped, it moves some channels by up to +79%).
recommendations.expected_impact: Up to \u20ac272k a month extra revenue at unchanged spend on long-history, good-fit lines; less after the cap. This is revenue, not gross profit.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Revenue \u00f7 paid spend over 28 days, compared with the 6.98 baseline.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM sales_daily WHERE day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM sales_daily),'-28 days'))/(SELECT SUM(spend) FROM ad_daily WHERE day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM ad_daily),'-28 days')) AS value

execution.note: Portfolio-wide, so Leadership approves. Each line's total stays the same. Money moves from Google brand and Meta retargeting to TikTok, creators, affiliates and YouTube, with no channel moving more than 25%. Mexico City has no model and is excluded. Lines with R\u00b2 below 0.5 (Paris Fashion and Beauty, the Amsterdam lines, most Beauty) should be watched closely.

recommendations.expected_impact: Brings back about \u20ac40k of revenue a week (about \u20ac170k a month).
recommendations.how_to_measure: Barcelona organic search sessions over the last 14 days (currently 101k) should move back toward about 165k.

input.brief: Data runs to 2026-11-01. Compare the 12 markets x 4 lines (Home, Fashion drops, Beauty, Gifts) over the last 4 weeks vs the prior 4 weeks and vs peers: revenue, gross profit, ROAS, CPA, conversion rate, share of potential demand captured (market_profile / search_interest). Flag market-lines capturing far less of their potential than peers, ads that are fatigued/broken/far above target CPA (with ad_ids, spend, n), and any funnel or stock problems (stock_events, product_daily) that marketing can't fix. Give numbers with n and euros at stake per month.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. Assess demand drivers per market-line: weather effect (rain etc. from weather_daily) measured per line with confidence — which lines have a clearly positive rain effect, which none/negative; holidays/seasonal (upcoming Nov peaks: Black Friday, Singles Day, Christmas run-up) so we don't mistake seasonality for problems; search_interest trends vs our sales. Give effect sizes, n, and which market-lines deserve a weather rule.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. Analyse voc_items/voc_labels for the last 4-8 weeks: top complaint themes by market and product (delivery, sizing, quality, checkout bugs, payment, stockouts), trend vs prior period, volume (n), and link to product_daily/returns/conversion where possible. Identify issues engineering/product/ops/logistics must fix (with market and product ids), and any products where a lifecycle email (back in stock, etc.) is warranted. Estimate euros at stake.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. Run/report the marketing-mix view: per market-line, model fit quality (R2/holdout), marginal ROAS by channel (Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Google, affiliates, creators), recommended channel split. Tell me where fit is good (how many of 48 market-lines), the expected gross profit gain from applying the split portfolio-wide with a per-channel cap, and which market-lines have high marginal ROAS + low demand capture (candidates for more budget) vs low marginal ROAS (funding sources). Also budget pacing vs plan (v_budget_pacing) and any overspend.

benchmark_analyst-1.text:
I've submitted the findings. The biggest problem is that iOS checkout broke in Paris and Amsterdam on 14 Oct, about €1.4M of lost revenue a month, and ads can't fix it. Several parts of the brief went unanswered because I ran out of turns (listed at the end).

**1. iOS checkout broke in Paris and Amsterdam (all four lines)**
- **What happened:** In both markets, the share of iOS checkouts that become orders dropped overnight on 14 Oct, from about 62% to about 22%. Paris went from 61.3% on 13 Oct to 21.5% on 14 Oct; Amsterdam from 61.8% to 20.8%. It has stayed there since.
- **Where it isn't happening:** Android and desktop stayed at 61–63%. Peer markets' iOS rate is 61.65–62.57%, and last year's was 62.0% (Paris) and 61.4% (Amsterdam).
- **How big:** Since 14 Oct, Paris had 25,731 iOS checkouts and 5,657 orders; Amsterdam had 11,350 checkouts and 2,504 orders. At the normal 62% rate, that's about €976k a month of lost revenue in Paris and €428k in Amsterdam. Average order is €60 in both.
- **Is it real:** Yes. The Paris drop is clearly beyond noise, even after correcting for the 36 comparisons scanned.
- **Knock-on effect:** It explains most of the ad cost-per-order rises in these two markets. For example, Amsterdam Fashion drops on Google went from €34.7 to €63.0 per order, Amsterdam Beauty retargeting from €36.8 to €63.6, and Paris Fashion drops on Meta from €26.3 to €42.6. These ads aren't broken; the orders are being lost at checkout.
- **Action:** Treat it as an engineering emergency (payment step and Apple Pay first, then look at whatever was released on 13–14 Oct). Also look at pausing iOS-heavy ads in these two markets until it's fixed.

**2. One ad is worn out: Berlin Gifts, Meta prospecting (BER-GFT-META-PROSPECTING)**
- Over the last 4 weeks it spent €13,797. People are seeing it twice as often (4.09 times on average vs 2.03), click rate fell from 1.18% to 0.85%, and orders fell from 533 to 316.
- Cost per order rose from €30.8 to €43.7, against a €25 target.
- That's about 132 lost orders a month, roughly €9k. That figure is a rough estimate: I didn't pull Berlin's own order value and used about €66, the Gifts average in Paris and Amsterdam.
- **Action:** Swap in new creative and broaden the audience.

**3. Mexico City launch is far behind earlier launches**
- Eight weeks in, it makes €1,999 a day, 5% of what Miami (€37,189) and São Paulo (€48,796) made at the same age.
- Cost per order is €36.30 against peers' €19.27–22.18. Several small ads have spent €600–2,100 for 3–19 orders each.
- **Action:** Before spending more, find out why demand isn't converting.

**Weaker signals (not sized)**
- **Milan:** returning customers' share of revenue fell to 8.1%, against 11.7% last year and peers at 11.5–13.3%. Worth checking CRM and email sends.
- **Barcelona:** organic share of revenue is 40.4%, against 46.2% last year and peers at 40.8–47.1%.

**Not problems**
- **Lisbon** has lower revenue than its peers, but it matches its own last year (€34.7k vs €35.8k a day) and the previous period (€36.0k). It's a smaller market.
- Small Android and desktop gaps (New York, London, Berlin, less than 0.6 points) are noise.
- Most prospecting ads cost €30–55 per order across all markets, so being above the €25 target isn't news on its own.

**Not covered:** gross profit (there's no margin data), share of potential demand captured, and stock problems. New York Home Meta prospecting (€31.3 → €47.5 per order) and some other New York ads got worse with no change in how often people see them or click. I didn't diagnose these, and they need a follow-up.

input.summary: Since 2026-10-14, iOS checkout has been broken in both Paris and Amsterdam. iOS checkout-to-order fell from about 62% to 34.7%, matching a new wave of complaints about declined cards and payments failing on phones. That puts about €1.4M a month at stake, and engineering should fix it first. The other new issues are broken Google links after a Barcelona site change (organic search −€5.3k/day) and late deliveries in Milan, where repeat buying has fallen below peers.

findings.title: iOS payment/checkout failure (cards declined, payment page freezes on phone)
findings.evidence: payment_problem is 12.1% of comments (26/214) vs 2.6% elsewhere and 1.8% before; NEW, p≈0. Fashion drops 14.0% (8/57). iOS checkout-to-order 61.9%→34.8% (37,878 checkouts, 13,182 orders); Android 61.8% and desktop 61.9% unchanged. All-device conversion 49.1% vs LY 61.9% and peers 61.9–62.1%. Below 50% every day since 2026-10-14 (19 days). Lost revenue vs 62% conversion is €32.5k/day.

findings.title: iOS payment/checkout failure (same bug as Paris)
findings.evidence: payment_problem is 15.5% of comments (33/213) vs 2.3% elsewhere and 2.8% before; NEW. iOS checkout-to-order 62.0%→34.7% (16,622 checkouts, 5,774 orders); Android and desktop about 62%. Started 2026-10-14. All-device 49.1% vs LY 61.7% and peers 61.9–62.2%. NPS fell from −1 to −17. Lost about €14.3k/day.

findings.title: Broken URLs / site search after a site change: organic search traffic lost
findings.evidence: website_ux is 16.7% of comments (37/221) vs 3.8% elsewhere and 5.3% before; NEW. Customers say Google links return errors since the site changed, and site search doesn't work. Organic search sessions fell from about 83k/week to about 50–55k/week starting the week of 2026-09-21. Organic search revenue per day: €14,679 before → €9,332 after. Organic share 40.4% vs LY 46.2% and peer median 45.5%.

findings.title: Late deliveries / tracking stuck; repeat purchases falling
findings.evidence: delivery_late is 24.2% of comments (54/223) vs 6.4% elsewhere and 5.1% before; NEW. Weekly count jumped from 2–5 to 19 in the week of 2026-10-05, then 14, 11, 10 (fading but not resolved). Customers report orders a week late and promised-Friday orders arriving the next Thursday. Repeat share 8.1% vs 11.3% previous period, LY 11.7%, peers 11.5–13.3%. Revenue per day €51,169 vs €53,725 previous period (within peer range). Euro figure ≈ (53,725 − 51,169) × 30.

findings.title: New market lacks brand trust
findings.evidence: trust_brand is 14.5% of comments (34/235) vs 3.1% elsewhere; persistent (13.8% before). Customers say they don't know the brand. NPS fell from −22 to −33. 8 weeks after launch, revenue is €1,999/day, 5% of what Miami and São Paulo made at the same age.

findings.title: Lisbon Fashion drop Edition 11 (LIS-FSH-E10) sold out; demand far above capacity
findings.evidence: sold_out event on 2026-10-21. Capacity 145, but 505 units recorded so far. Daily units went from 46–59 to 26–39 after selling out. Exit comments say customers left because the item was sold out. However, Lisbon's sold_out mentions are flat (13 now vs 11 before), so this is not statistically significant.

findings.title: Paris Home customers ask for more range (long-standing)
findings.evidence: wants_more_range is 17.0% of comments (9/53) vs 3.0% elsewhere; not new (19.3% before). Paris NPS steady at −31.

proposed_actions.action: Engineering: open a P0 for iOS checkout/payment in Paris and Amsterdam. Check what changed in the payment SDK, 3DS or the PSP around 2026-10-14 (iOS app or Safari web). Then email customers who abandoned checkout to come back and finish the purchase.
proposed_actions.why: iOS conversion fell from about 62% to 35% on the same day in both markets while other devices held steady. About €1.4M a month at stake.

proposed_actions.action: Web/SEO: add 301 redirects from the old Barcelona URLs, resubmit the sitemap and fix site search.
proposed_actions.why: Organic search sessions are down about 35% since 2026-09-21. About €5.3k/day of organic search revenue lost.

proposed_actions.action: Logistics: escalate with the Milan carrier or warehouse, which slipped from the week of 2026-10-05. Send proactive delay emails and service-recovery codes to affected Milan buyers.
proposed_actions.why: Late-delivery complaints are about 5× baseline, and repeat share has fallen below every peer.

proposed_actions.action: Marketing (Mexico City): add trust signals (reviews, local payment/returns guarantees, press, PR) before scaling spend.
proposed_actions.why: Distrust of an unknown brand accounts for 14.5% of comments, and the launch is tracking at 5% of earlier launches.

proposed_actions.action: Lifecycle/merch: send a back-in-stock / waitlist email for LIS-FSH-E10 if a restock is possible; otherwise send a next-drop alert to Lisbon Fashion visitors.
proposed_actions.why: The product sold out on 2026-10-21 with demand far above its 145-unit capacity, and daily sales roughly halved afterwards.

not_problems: Returns/refunds, product quality, sizing and sold-out complaints are flat or low single digits per market (for example, sizing 8–12 per market both periods). This is noise, not a new issue. Milan and Mexico City product-quality mentions actually fell.
Milan revenue per day (€51.2k) is within the peer range (€36.7k–€63.2k). The concern there is repeat buying and NPS, not a revenue collapse.
Miami NPS improved from −25 to −5, and London is stable at −6.
Amsterdam and Paris Android and desktop conversion are normal (about 62%), so the checkout problem is iOS-only and not a demand problem.
Paris Home 'wants more range' is a long-standing theme (19.3% before), not a new problem.

input.summary: The model's channel split adds an expected €135,004 a week in revenue (about €585k a month) across the 19 largest market-lines it showed. Only €62,671 a week of that comes from long-history market-lines with good fit, and the plan moves some channels by up to +79%, past its own ±50% cap. Separately, London overspent its October budget by €81,179 (122.5%), mostly on Google brand and Meta retargeting, where an extra euro returns less than €1.

findings.title: Model fit: 24 of 44 modelled market-lines fit well (R² ≥ 0.7); 8 of those 24 have short histories; Mexico City has no model
findings.evidence: R² ≥ 0.7 (24): NY ×4 (0.764–0.96), São Paulo ×4 (0.984–0.991, 42 weeks), Miami ×4 (0.987–0.993, 32 weeks), Madrid Home 0.757 and Gifts 0.93, Lisbon Home 0.787 and Gifts 0.93, London Home 0.762 and Gifts 0.932, Berlin Fashion 0.733 and Gifts 0.924, Barcelona Gifts 0.875, Paris Gifts 0.862, Milan Gifts 0.945, Amsterdam Gifts 0.755. R² 0.5–0.7 (9). R² below 0.5 (11): Paris Beauty 0.188, Paris Fashion 0.228, London Beauty 0.243, Amsterdam Beauty 0.243, Amsterdam Home 0.325, Madrid Beauty 0.356, Lisbon Fashion 0.362, Amsterdam Fashion 0.367, Berlin Beauty 0.422, Milan Fashion 0.453, Barcelona Fashion 0.489. Gifts fits well in every market; Beauty fits worst. São Paulo and Miami show R² near 0.99 on 32–42 weeks of data with 8 channels plus search as inputs, so they are probably overfitted. No holdout or uncertainty range is available from the tool. The pooled Meta prospecting elasticity (0.9747) is nearly identical to the search elasticity (~0.97), a sign that Meta prospecting is hard to separate from search demand.

findings.title: Reallocation plan: +€135,004/week revenue across the 19 largest lines shown; €62,671/week is on reliable fits
findings.evidence: Sum of expected weekly gains for the 19 market-lines the tool returned (output was cut off after that) = €135,004/week, about €585k/month, at unchanged total spend. The other 25 lines each gain ≤ €4,927/week. By fit: R² ≥ 0.7 lines = €99,511/week, of which €36,840 is São Paulo and Miami (likely overfit), leaving €62,671/week (about €272k/month) on long-history, good-fit lines (NY Home €10,846, London Home €10,032, NY Fashion €8,846, London Gifts €8,361, Paris Gifts €7,608, Madrid Home €6,185, NY Gifts €5,567, NY Beauty €5,226). Mid-fit lines €22,704/week; poor-fit lines €12,789/week (Paris Fashion R² 0.228 €7,804, Barcelona Fashion €4,985). These are revenue figures, not gross profit: no margin data exists in the hub. The plan also breaks its stated ±50% cap, with increases of +55% to +79% on TikTok, YouTube, affiliates and creators, so capped gains will be lower.

findings.title: Saturated channels: Google brand and Meta retargeting return well under €1 per extra euro
findings.evidence: Google brand marginal ROAS 0.07–0.62 in most European and NY lines (e.g. Barcelona Gifts 0.07, Paris Gifts 0.08, Amsterdam Gifts 0.10, Lisbon Beauty 0.12). Meta retargeting 0.13–0.8 (Amsterdam Beauty 0.13, Amsterdam Fashion 0.15, London Fashion 0.29). Yet last-click first-party ROAS is 9.03 for Google brand: it collects demand that would arrive anyway. Exceptions: in São Paulo and Miami these channels still return 1.06–1.97.

findings.title: Under-funded channels: TikTok, creators, affiliates and YouTube return €3–8 per extra euro on small budgets
findings.evidence: Marginal ROAS: TikTok up to 8.08 (São Paulo Gifts), 6.09 (NY Home), 5.53 (London Home); creators 5.88 (Paris Gifts), 5.62 (NY Home); affiliates 6.44 (Paris Home). Weekly spend on each is only about €600–2,500 per line, against €3,300–8,000 on Meta prospecting.

findings.title: Platforms over-claim, most on Meta retargeting, YouTube and TikTok
findings.evidence: Last 28 days, platform ROAS vs first-party ROAS: Meta retargeting 3.43 vs 1.56 (2.2×), and the model's marginal ROAS is mostly below 1. YouTube 5.90 vs 3.02 and TikTok 5.81 vs 3.24 (about 1.8–2×), but the model still puts their marginal ROAS at 3–6, so they remain under-funded despite the inflated claims. Meta prospecting 2.45 vs 1.72.

findings.title: Lines where an extra euro earns most vs lines to fund from
findings.evidence: Blended marginal ROAS. Candidates for more budget: São Paulo Gifts 3.03, São Paulo Home 2.93, Miami Home 2.83 (all short-history fits), Paris Home 2.60 (R² 0.591), Madrid Home 2.31 (R² 0.757), NY Home 2.16 (R² 0.909), London Home 2.13 (R² 0.762). Funding sources: Amsterdam Beauty 0.82, Lisbon Beauty 0.99, Amsterdam Fashion 1.06, Barcelona Beauty 1.07, Milan Beauty 1.12, Amsterdam Gifts 1.13, Paris Beauty 1.15, Madrid Beauty 1.16. The tools give no demand-capture metric, so that part of the screen could not be applied.

findings.title: London overspent October by €81,179 (122.5% of budget), mostly in saturated channels
findings.evidence: October spend €441,179 against a €360,000 budget; August and September were 99.6% and 98.4%. September-to-October increases include Google brand (Beauty +€5,993, Home +€5,111, Fashion +€4,044, Gifts +€3,014) and Meta retargeting (Gifts +€4,865, Fashion +€3,542); London's marginal ROAS on these is 0.19–0.72. London's spend is up 14.9% over the last 28 days while paid revenue rose 3.4% and organic fell 1.7%.

findings.title: Smaller October overspends: Barcelona 109.5%, Lisbon 107.1%
findings.evidence: Barcelona €280,377 against €256,000 (+€24,377); Lisbon €214,292 against €200,000 (+€14,292). October's 31 days explain only about 3 points; most markets landed at 101–104%. On the first November day Barcelona is projecting 109.1% again.

findings.title: Organic revenue down about 21% vs last year in Amsterdam, Paris and Barcelona
findings.evidence: Organic vs last year: Amsterdam −21.6%, Paris −21.3%, Barcelona −21.1%, with spend flat to +8.5%. Amsterdam's MER is the lowest of the established markets at 4.78. This is a demand problem, not a media one, so pass it to brand/search.

proposed_actions.action: Start the channel split only on long-history, good-fit lines: NY Home, Fashion, Gifts and Beauty; London Home and Gifts; Paris Gifts; Madrid Home. Cut Google brand and Meta retargeting by about 40–46% (e.g. NY Home retargeting €3,214→€1,871/week and brand €3,112→€1,812/week). Move that money to TikTok, YouTube, affiliates and creators, re-capped at +50%.
proposed_actions.why: These lines carry €62,671/week (about €272k/month) of the plan's expected revenue gain on R² 0.76–0.96. The cap needs re-running because the current plan reaches +79%.

proposed_actions.action: For São Paulo, Miami and the poor-fit lines (Paris Fashion and Beauty, Amsterdam, all Beauty below R² 0.5), test before moving money: geo-holdout or turn-off tests on Google brand and Meta retargeting, plus incremental tests on TikTok and creators.
proposed_actions.why: R² near 0.99 on 32–42 weeks is likely overfit, and R² below 0.5 cannot rank channels. The model's estimate here could be off by more than the gain.

proposed_actions.action: Pull London back to its €360k November budget, starting with the October additions to Google brand (+€18,162 across lines) and Meta retargeting.
proposed_actions.why: October overspend was €81,179 on channels where an extra euro returns €0.19–0.72.

proposed_actions.action: Shift some budget from Beauty lines with marginal ROAS ≤ 1.16 (Amsterdam, Lisbon, Barcelona, Milan, Paris, Madrid) toward Home lines at 2.1–2.6 (Madrid, NY, London, Paris).
proposed_actions.why: The same euro is expected to earn about twice as much revenue. Confirm with margin data first: gains here are revenue, not gross profit.

proposed_actions.action: Rebuild the model with a holdout and confidence intervals, and add margins.
proposed_actions.why: There is no holdout or error range today, and the brief asks for gross profit, which the hub cannot produce.

output.summary: Rain moves demand reliably for Home (+9% to +18%) and Gifts (+12% to +33%) in every market, does not move Beauty in any useful way (−0.5% to +4%), and lowers Fashion drops (−4% to −14%). That supports rain rules on 23 Home and Gifts market-lines and a "pull back" rule on Fashion drops. The largest missed demand is Paris Home (64% of potential, +€1.17M gap over 8 weeks, marginal ROAS 2.6) and Mexico City at launch (about 50% of potential), but part of the Paris gap is a checkout fault across all Paris lines (55.5% vs 61.9% for peers). That fault also cuts into Paris's weather and holiday upside.

findings.title: Paris Home under-captures search demand: likely a reach or budget gap, made worse by a checkout fault
findings.evidence: demand_potential: 14.24 orders per 1,000 category searches vs 22.11 for peers, so 64% of potential is captured. The gap is 15,868 orders, €1,173,755 over 8 weeks. Other Paris lines capture 89–92%, so the shortfall is mostly specific to Home. Marginal ROAS is 2.6 (4th best of 44 cells), with affiliates' marginal ROAS at 6.44, so this looks like a reach or budget gap. Checkout-to-order is 55.18% vs a peer median of 61.89% and 61.93% last year (all Paris lines: 55.48%), and revenue per day is €33,966 vs €38,789 last year. Part of the gap is therefore a conversion problem for the checkout specialist. Monthly figure = €1.17M ÷ 8 weeks × 4.35, and should be read as an upper bound.

findings.title: Paris revenue is down 10–14.5% year on year in every line while search is flat, which points to checkout, not demand
findings.evidence: Revenue vs search interest, last 8 weeks year on year: Gifts −14.5% vs −4.3%, Fashion drops −12.1% vs +1.3%, Home −12.0% vs −2.9%, Beauty −9.9% vs +4.9%. Checkout-to-order is 55.48% vs 61.96% last year and the previous period, outside the peer range of 61.82–62.04. Demand did not fall, so Paris capture rates and forecasted uplifts are understated until checkout is fixed.

findings.title: Mexico City launch captures about half of its search demand
findings.evidence: Captured share: Home 51%, Fashion drops 48%, Gifts 52%, Beauty 51%. Capture is 9.7–11.5 orders per 1,000 searches vs 20–22 for peers. The combined 8-week gap is €385k (€114,685 + €110,442 + €92,159 + €67,735). At 8 weeks old, revenue is €1,999/day, 5% of earlier launches at the same age (Miami €37,189, São Paulo €48,796). MER is 5.39 vs a peer median of 7.81. There is no marginal-returns data for Mexico City yet. Monthly figure is a conversion of the 8-week gap.

findings.title: Rain effect is clearly positive for Home and Gifts in all markets (weather rule candidates)
findings.evidence: n = 434 days (São Paulo 300, Miami 229–230). The 95% range excludes zero in every Home and Gifts cell. Strongest: Paris Gifts +32.8% [29.5, 36.1], Milan Gifts +31.8% [28.1, 35.6], Berlin Gifts +27.2% [24.0, 30.6], Barcelona Home +17.7% [14.8, 20.7], London Gifts +17.6% [14.3, 20.9], London Home +17.1% [14.8, 19.6], Berlin Home +16.9%, São Paulo Gifts +16.7% [11.8, 21.9]. Weakest: Miami Home +9.3% [2.4, 16.7], which is a wide range and flagged not rain-sensitive in the outlook.

findings.title: Rain lowers Fashion drops demand in every market
findings.evidence: Every 95% range is below zero: Miami −14.0% [−18.8, −8.9], Berlin −7.9% [−9.8, −5.9], London −7.2% [−9.0, −5.3], Barcelona −6.8% [−9.0, −4.5], Milan −5.8%, São Paulo −5.5% [−9.8, −1.0], Lisbon −5.0%, Amsterdam −4.8%, Paris −4.7%, New York −4.6%, Madrid −4.0% [−6.6, −1.3].

findings.title: Beauty: rain effect is none or too small to act on
findings.evidence: The range includes zero in Madrid (+2.3%), Lisbon (+2.2%), London (+1.8%), Berlin (+2.2%), Amsterdam (+2.4% [−0.0, 5.0]), São Paulo (+2.2%) and Miami (+0.2%). Barcelona (+3.3%), Paris (+2.8%), Milan (+2.7%) and New York (+4.1%) are only marginally above zero. All of these are below the demand model's 7.5% error, so no rule is warranted.

findings.title: Next 14 days (2–15 Nov): rain-driven uplift is concentrated in São Paulo, Paris, Iberia and Milan
findings.evidence: demand_outlook expected extra revenue: São Paulo Gifts +€35,465 (+11.3%, 8 rainy days), São Paulo Home +€32,543 (+8.4%), Paris Gifts +€27,977 (+10.4%), Barcelona Home +€20,944 (+8.8%, 7 rainy days), Paris Home +€19,965, Milan Gifts +€19,112 (+10.7%), Madrid Home +€17,581, Madrid Gifts +€15,544, Miami Gifts +€14,696. Paris upside will only fully land if checkout recovers. Model holdout accuracy: MAPE 7.5%, 84% of 352 predictions within 10%.

findings.title: November–December seasonality: Gifts and Home ramp up, Fashion drops eases off
findings.market: established markets (excluding Miami, São Paulo, Mexico City)
findings.evidence: Revenue per day last year: Gifts €148,691 (Oct 2025) → €208,194 (Nov) → €293,898 (Dec) → €158,970 (Jan). The step up came in the week of 1 Dec 2025 (€310,580 vs €208,876 the week before). Home: €194,056 → €235,515 → €261,588. Beauty: €114,861 → €121,775 → €150,581. Fashion drops: €189,116 (Sep) → €163,110 (Oct) → €157,194 (Nov) → €155,567 (Dec). The week of Singles Day (10 Nov) shows a small lift (Gifts €211,014, Home €241,359). Public holidays: Gifts +5.7% to +16.7%, Home +3.6% to +16.7%. Fashion drops and Beauty are mostly flat or negative (e.g. New York Beauty −6.9%, Amsterdam Beauty −6.0%, London Beauty −5.5%).

proposed_actions.action: Turn on a rain rule (raise bids and budget when rain is forecast) for Gifts in Paris, Milan, Berlin, São Paulo, London and Miami, and for Home in Barcelona, London, Berlin, Milan, New York and Paris. Leave Miami Home out until its range narrows.
proposed_actions.why: Each has a rain effect of +15% to +33% with a 95% range well above zero over 229–434 days, and the next 14 days show €11k–35k of extra revenue per cell.

proposed_actions.action: Add the reverse rule for Fashion drops: on rainy days, shift spend and drop launches away from Fashion drops, toward Home and Gifts in the same market (start with Miami, Berlin, London and Barcelona).
proposed_actions.why: Rain lowers Fashion drops orders by 4% to 14% in every market, with ranges below zero.

proposed_actions.action: Increase Paris Home reach (affiliates, with marginal ROAS 6.44) only once the Paris checkout fault has been handed off and fixed.
proposed_actions.why: 64% captured share and marginal ROAS 2.6 point to a budget gap, but checkout-to-order at 55% vs 62% would waste part of any extra spend.

proposed_actions.action: Review Mexico City launch reach and spend vs the Miami and São Paulo launch plans.
proposed_actions.why: About 50% captured share and 5% of earlier launches' revenue at the same age, with no marginal-returns read yet.

proposed_actions.action: Plan November budgets on last year's ramp: Gifts and Home step up from the week of 1 Dec, with a small Singles Day lift. Don't count Fashion drops' Oct–Dec softness as a problem.
proposed_actions.why: Last year Gifts nearly doubled from Oct to Dec while Fashion drops eased.

proposed_actions.action: Do not build weather rules for Beauty. If budget needs to move, Beauty in Amsterdam (0.82), Lisbon (0.99) and Barcelona (1.07) are the lowest marginal-ROAS donors.
proposed_actions.why: Beauty's rain effect is ≤4% and inside the model's error, and its marginal returns are the lowest of the four lines.

not_problems: Fashion drops falling from €189k/day in Sep to about €156k/day in Nov–Dec happened last year too: it is seasonal and gets worse on rainy days.

Amsterdam revenue is down 6.5–10.6% year on year by line (€41,692/day vs €46,139), but that is inside the peer range (€35,339–55,806) and captured share is 96–101%. This is not a demand gap; keep watching it.
Madrid Beauty (109%), Lisbon Home (114%), Berlin Home (108%) and New York Home (103%) capture above peers. They are saturated, not under-served.
Small year-on-year search moves (Beauty +1.4%, Fashion drops +0.9%, Home −0.9%, Gifts −2.8% across established markets) are noise. The revenue drop beyond that comes mainly from Paris's checkout.
Weather effects under about 7% (all of Beauty) are inside the demand model's 7.5% MAPE and should not trigger rules.
Holiday dips in Beauty and Fashion drops (e.g. New York Beauty −6.9%, London Fashion drops −4.6%) are normal holiday behaviour, not faults.

output.summary: Since 2026-10-14, iOS checkout has been broken in both Paris and Amsterdam. iOS checkout-to-order fell from about 62% to 34.7%, matching a new wave of complaints about declined cards and payments failing on phones. That puts about €1.4M a month at stake, and engineering should fix it first. The other new issues are broken Google links after a Barcelona site change (organic search −€5.3k/day) and late deliveries in Milan, where repeat buying has fallen below peers.

findings.evidence: payment_problem is 12.1% of comments (26/214) vs 2.6% elsewhere and 1.8% before; NEW, p≈0. Fashion drops 14.0% (8/57). iOS checkout-to-order 61.9%→34.8% (37,878 checkouts, 13,182 orders); Android 61.8% and desktop 61.9% unchanged. All-device conversion 49.1% vs LY 61.9% and peers 61.9–62.1%. Below 50% every day since 2026-10-14 (19 days). Lost revenue vs 62% conversion is €32.5k/day.

findings.title: iOS payment/checkout failure (same bug as Paris)
findings.evidence: payment_problem is 15.5% of comments (33/213) vs 2.3% elsewhere and 2.8% before; NEW. iOS checkout-to-order 62.0%→34.7% (16,622 checkouts, 5,774 orders); Android and desktop about 62%. Started 2026-10-14. All-device 49.1% vs LY 61.7% and peers 61.9–62.2%. NPS fell from −1 to −17. Lost about €14.3k/day.

findings.title: Broken URLs / site search after a site change: organic search traffic lost
findings.evidence: website_ux is 16.7% of comments (37/221) vs 3.8% elsewhere and 5.3% before; NEW. Customers say Google links return errors since the site changed, and site search doesn't work. Organic search sessions fell from about 83k/week to about 50–55k/week starting the week of 2026-09-21. Organic search revenue per day: €14,679 before → €9,332 after. Organic share 40.4% vs LY 46.2% and peer median 45.5%.

findings.title: Late deliveries / tracking stuck; repeat purchases falling
findings.evidence: delivery_late is 24.2% of comments (54/223) vs 6.4% elsewhere and 5.1% before; NEW. Weekly count jumped from 2–5 to 19 in the week of 2026-10-05, then 14, 11, 10 (fading but not resolved). Customers report orders a week late and promised-Friday orders arriving the next Thursday. Repeat share 8.1% vs 11.3% previous period, LY 11.7%, peers 11.5–13.3%. Revenue per day €51,169 vs €53,725 previous period (within peer range). Euro figure ≈ (53,725 − 51,169) × 30.

findings.title: New market lacks brand trust
findings.evidence: trust_brand is 14.5% of comments (34/235) vs 3.1% elsewhere; persistent (13.8% before). Customers say they don't know the brand. NPS fell from −22 to −33. 8 weeks after launch, revenue is €1,999/day, 5% of what Miami and São Paulo made at the same age.

findings.title: Lisbon Fashion drop Edition 11 (LIS-FSH-E10) sold out; demand far above capacity
findings.evidence: sold_out event on 2026-10-21. Capacity 145, but 505 units recorded so far. Daily units went from 46–59 to 26–39 after selling out. Exit comments say customers left because the item was sold out. However, Lisbon's sold_out mentions are flat (13 now vs 11 before), so this is not statistically significant.

findings.title: Paris Home customers ask for more range (long-standing)
findings.evidence: wants_more_range is 17.0% of comments (9/53) vs 3.0% elsewhere; not new (19.3% before). Paris NPS steady at −31.

proposed_actions.action: Engineering: open a P0 for iOS checkout/payment in Paris and Amsterdam. Check what changed in the payment SDK, 3DS or the PSP around 2026-10-14 (iOS app or Safari web). Then email customers who abandoned checkout to come back and finish the purchase.
proposed_actions.why: iOS conversion fell from about 62% to 35% on the same day in both markets while other devices held steady. About €1.4M a month at stake.

proposed_actions.action: Web/SEO: add 301 redirects from the old Barcelona URLs, resubmit the sitemap and fix site search.
proposed_actions.why: Organic search sessions are down about 35% since 2026-09-21. About €5.3k/day of organic search revenue lost.

proposed_actions.action: Logistics: escalate with the Milan carrier or warehouse, which slipped from the week of 2026-10-05. Send proactive delay emails and service-recovery codes to affected Milan buyers.
proposed_actions.why: Late-delivery complaints are about 5× baseline, and repeat share has fallen below every peer.

proposed_actions.action: Marketing (Mexico City): add trust signals (reviews, local payment/returns guarantees, press, PR) before scaling spend.
proposed_actions.why: Distrust of an unknown brand accounts for 14.5% of comments, and the launch is tracking at 5% of earlier launches.

proposed_actions.action: Lifecycle/merch: send a back-in-stock / waitlist email for LIS-FSH-E10 if a restock is possible; otherwise send a next-drop alert to Lisbon Fashion visitors.
proposed_actions.why: The product sold out on 2026-10-21 with demand far above its 145-unit capacity, and daily sales roughly halved afterwards.

not_problems: Returns/refunds, product quality, sizing and sold-out complaints are flat or low single digits per market (for example, sizing 8–12 per market both periods). This is noise, not a new issue. Milan and Mexico City product-quality mentions actually fell.

Miami NPS improved from −25 to −5, and London is stable at −6.

output.summary: The model's channel split adds an expected €135,004 a week in revenue (about €585k a month) across the 19 largest market-lines it showed. Only €62,671 a week of that comes from long-history market-lines with good fit, and the plan moves some channels by up to +79%, past its own ±50% cap. Separately, London overspent its October budget by €81,179 (122.5%), mostly on Google brand and Meta retargeting, where an extra euro returns less than €1.

findings.title: Model fit: 24 of 44 modelled market-lines fit well (R² ≥ 0.7); 8 of those 24 have short histories; Mexico City has no model
findings.evidence: R² ≥ 0.7 (24): NY ×4 (0.764–0.96), São Paulo ×4 (0.984–0.991, 42 weeks), Miami ×4 (0.987–0.993, 32 weeks), Madrid Home 0.757 and Gifts 0.93, Lisbon Home 0.787 and Gifts 0.93, London Home 0.762 and Gifts 0.932, Berlin Fashion 0.733 and Gifts 0.924, Barcelona Gifts 0.875, Paris Gifts 0.862, Milan Gifts 0.945, Amsterdam Gifts 0.755. R² 0.5–0.7 (9). R² below 0.5 (11): Paris Beauty 0.188, Paris Fashion 0.228, London Beauty 0.243, Amsterdam Beauty 0.243, Amsterdam Home 0.325, Madrid Beauty 0.356, Lisbon Fashion 0.362, Amsterdam Fashion 0.367, Berlin Beauty 0.422, Milan Fashion 0.453, Barcelona Fashion 0.489. Gifts fits well in every market; Beauty fits worst. São Paulo and Miami show R² near 0.99 on 32–42 weeks of data with 8 channels plus search as inputs, so they are probably overfitted. No holdout or uncertainty range is available from the tool. The pooled Meta prospecting elasticity (0.9747) is nearly identical to the search elasticity (~0.97), a sign that Meta prospecting is hard to separate from search demand.

findings.title: Reallocation plan: +€135,004/week revenue across the 19 largest lines shown; €62,671/week is on reliable fits
findings.evidence: Sum of expected weekly gains for the 19 market-lines the tool returned (output was cut off after that) = €135,004/week, about €585k/month, at unchanged total spend. The other 25 lines each gain ≤ €4,927/week. By fit: R² ≥ 0.7 lines = €99,511/week, of which €36,840 is São Paulo and Miami (likely overfit), leaving €62,671/week (about €272k/month) on long-history, good-fit lines (NY Home €10,846, London Home €10,032, NY Fashion €8,846, London Gifts €8,361, Paris Gifts €7,608, Madrid Home €6,185, NY Gifts €5,567, NY Beauty €5,226). Mid-fit lines €22,704/week; poor-fit lines €12,789/week (Paris Fashion R² 0.228 €7,804, Barcelona Fashion €4,985). These are revenue figures, not gross profit: no margin data exists in the hub. The plan also breaks its stated ±50% cap, with increases of +55% to +79% on TikTok, YouTube, affiliates and creators, so capped gains will be lower.

findings.title: Saturated channels: Google brand and Meta retargeting return well under €1 per extra euro
findings.evidence: Google brand marginal ROAS 0.07–0.62 in most European and NY lines (e.g. Barcelona Gifts 0.07, Paris Gifts 0.08, Amsterdam Gifts 0.10, Lisbon Beauty 0.12). Meta retargeting 0.13–0.8 (Amsterdam Beauty 0.13, Amsterdam Fashion 0.15, London Fashion 0.29). Yet last-click first-party ROAS is 9.03 for Google brand: it collects demand that would arrive anyway. Exceptions: in São Paulo and Miami these channels still return 1.06–1.97.

findings.title: Under-funded channels: TikTok, creators, affiliates and YouTube return €3–8 per extra euro on small budgets
findings.evidence: Marginal ROAS: TikTok up to 8.08 (São Paulo Gifts), 6.09 (NY Home), 5.53 (London Home); creators 5.88 (Paris Gifts), 5.62 (NY Home); affiliates 6.44 (Paris Home). Weekly spend on each is only about €600–2,500 per line, against €3,300–8,000 on Meta prospecting.

findings.title: Platforms over-claim, most on Meta retargeting, YouTube and TikTok
findings.evidence: Last 28 days, platform ROAS vs first-party ROAS: Meta retargeting 3.43 vs 1.56 (2.2×), and the model's marginal ROAS is mostly below 1. YouTube 5.90 vs 3.02 and TikTok 5.81 vs 3.24 (about 1.8–2×), but the model still puts their marginal ROAS at 3–6, so they remain under-funded despite the inflated claims. Meta prospecting 2.45 vs 1.72.

findings.title: Lines where an extra euro earns most vs lines to fund from
findings.evidence: Blended marginal ROAS. Candidates for more budget: São Paulo Gifts 3.03, São Paulo Home 2.93, Miami Home 2.83 (all short-history fits), Paris Home 2.60 (R² 0.591), Madrid Home 2.31 (R² 0.757), NY Home 2.16 (R² 0.909), London Home 2.13 (R² 0.762). Funding sources: Amsterdam Beauty 0.82, Lisbon Beauty 0.99, Amsterdam Fashion 1.06, Barcelona Beauty 1.07, Milan Beauty 1.12, Amsterdam Gifts 1.13, Paris Beauty 1.15, Madrid Beauty 1.16. The tools give no demand-capture metric, so that part of the screen could not be applied.

findings.title: London overspent October by €81,179 (122.5% of budget), mostly in saturated channels
findings.evidence: October spend €441,179 against a €360,000 budget; August and September were 99.6% and 98.4%. September-to-October increases include Google brand (Beauty +€5,993, Home +€5,111, Fashion +€4,044, Gifts +€3,014) and Meta retargeting (Gifts +€4,865, Fashion +€3,542); London's marginal ROAS on these is 0.19–0.72. London's spend is up 14.9% over the last 28 days while paid revenue rose 3.4% and organic fell 1.7%.

findings.title: Smaller October overspends: Barcelona 109.5%, Lisbon 107.1%
findings.evidence: Barcelona €280,377 against €256,000 (+€24,377); Lisbon €214,292 against €200,000 (+€14,292). October's 31 days explain only about 3 points; most markets landed at 101–104%. On the first November day Barcelona is projecting 109.1% again.

findings.title: Organic revenue down about 21% vs last year in Amsterdam, Paris and Barcelona
findings.evidence: Organic vs last year: Amsterdam −21.6%, Paris −21.3%, Barcelona −21.1%, with spend flat to +8.5%. Amsterdam's MER is the lowest of the established markets at 4.78. This is a demand problem, not a media one, so pass it to brand/search.

proposed_actions.action: Start the channel split only on long-history, good-fit lines: NY Home, Fashion, Gifts and Beauty; London Home and Gifts; Paris Gifts; Madrid Home. Cut Google brand and Meta retargeting by about 40–46% (e.g. NY Home retargeting €3,214→€1,871/week and brand €3,112→€1,812/week). Move that money to TikTok, YouTube, affiliates and creators, re-capped at +50%.
proposed_actions.why: These lines carry €62,671/week (about €272k/month) of the plan's expected revenue gain on R² 0.76–0.96. The cap needs re-running because the current plan reaches +79%.

proposed_actions.action: For São Paulo, Miami and the poor-fit lines (Paris Fashion and Beauty, Amsterdam, all Beauty below R² 0.5), test before moving money: geo-holdout or turn-off tests on Google brand and Meta retargeting, plus incremental tests on TikTok and creators.
proposed_actions.why: R² near 0.99 on 32–42 weeks is likely overfit, and R² below 0.5 cannot rank channels. The model's estimate here could be off by more than the gain.

proposed_actions.action: Pull London back to its €360k November budget, starting with the October additions to Google brand (+€18,162 across lines) and Meta retargeting.
proposed_actions.why: October overspend was €81,179 on channels where an extra euro returns €0.19–0.72.

proposed_actions.action: Shift some budget from Beauty lines with marginal ROAS ≤ 1.16 (Amsterdam, Lisbon, Barcelona, Milan, Paris, Madrid) toward Home lines at 2.1–2.6 (Madrid, NY, London, Paris).
proposed_actions.why: The same euro is expected to earn about twice as much revenue. Confirm with margin data first: gains here are revenue, not gross profit.

proposed_actions.action: Rebuild the model with a holdout and confidence intervals, and add margins.
proposed_actions.why: There is no holdout or error range today, and the brief asks for gross profit, which the hub cannot produce.

not_problems: Mexico City at 27.3% projected November pacing, with October at 21.5% of budget and organic +214%: it is a new market ramping up (spend only began in September). There is not enough history to model it, so it is excluded from the 44.

New York organic −21.9% vs the prior 28 days is only −1.2% vs last year, so it is the usual seasonal pattern.
Monthly spend at 101–104% of budget in October for most markets is mostly October's 31 days.
